text:
sam: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection change landed yesterday I'm seeing a regression: ~2x OOM rate on 16GB nodes for long-sequence workloads (seq=1024..2048). Repro steps below, and perf traces attached.
maya: same on canary. KV cache fragmentation metric (slab_util_variance) jumped ~38% around the deploy. Prefill hit-rate dropped ~12% which increases decode pressure.
jon: Interesting — do we know if prefill is being favored over on-demand decode now? The new kernel routing might be biasing toward fast-prefill paths that allocate larger slabs.
sam: hypothesis: routing->kernel picks a prefilling kernel that requests contiguous workspace > thincap, causing more slab splits and fragmentation. When per-request cap kicks in, eviction path uses full-evict instead of demote, so we see OOMs.
alisa: saw related traces. Perfbot uploaded a hotspot profile (link: https://perf.internal/runs/4123) showing many small allocations from kv_prefill_path and high memcpy churn during demote.
perfbot: automated profile summary:
- P50 latency: +4ms on prefills
- GPU mem alloc churn +62%
- Top alloc callers: kv::prefill(), allocator::alloc_slab(), kernel::prepare_workspace()

jon: Proposed mitigation: hybrid eviction that prefers demotion->thincap packs before full eviction, and a soft per-request workspace cap that defers prefill when frag>threshold. Two knobs:
- demote_first=true
- per_request_soft_cap=0.7 (fraction of node soft reserve)

maya: would like to add a slab-coalescing pass on free-list when fragmentation passes 0.25 to avoid long-lived tiny holes being kept. Cheap compaction during low utilization windows.

sam: repro curl (short):
```
curl -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-8b\",\"input_len\":2048,\"batch\":4,\"mode\":\"stream\"}'
```
Logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:21Z] allocator: alloc_slab(16384) -> slab(0x7f8a)
[2026-03-15T03:12:21Z] kv: prefill hit=false, alloc_frag=0.42
[2026-03-15T03:12:21Z] oom: node=gpu-16-03, free_bytes=120MB, request=220MB
```

alisa: safe rollout plan: (1) enable demote_first on canary pool (5% traffic) with stat collection, (2) enable per_request_soft_cap=0.65 in canary, (3) add slab-coalesce background job at low QPS, (4) monitor OOMs, p50/p95, and slab_util_variance for 48h.

jon: A/B metrics to track: OOM count, prefill_hit_rate, decode_tokens_per_request, memcpy_bytes, slab_util_variance, avg_free_chunk_size. Also add an alert if p95 latency regresses >7%.

maya: I'll add a short perf test to the nightly harness to replay seq=1536/2048 streams and capture allocator traces. Sam, can you drop the config snippets you used for reproducer? I'll wire the canary change.

sam: pasted below — these are the node-level overrides I used for the canary test:
```
allocator:
  soft_reserve: 0.8  # fraction of GPU mem used as soft reserve
  per_request_soft_cap: 0.7
  demote_first: true
  coalesce_threshold: 0.25
kv:
  prefill_policy: auto
  prefer_on_demand_decode: false
```

maya: ack — will push canary rollout tomorrow 09:00 UTC. I'll also add a metric dashboard tile for slab_coalesce_runs and recent_coalesce_win_bytes.

jon: one more thought — add a microbenchmark to ensure kernel-selection doesn't blow up contiguous workspace size. If kernel heuristics pick different workspace requirements based on batch packing, we should include those cases.

alisa: assigning owners: maya=canary rollout + dashboards, jon=bench + kernel testcase, sam=repro harness + traces, me(alisa)=monitoring/alerts config. We'll reconvene after 24h of canary data.

sam: thanks — filing a short follow-up ticket with the experiment details and perf links. :thumbsup:
